arguments.value: 47-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, schizoaffective disorder/depression/ADHD, and recurrent alcohol-related hospitalizations presented with coffee-ground emesis, acute blood loss anemia, and acute kidney injury after heavy drinking. He had been treated outpatient with multiple AUD medications simultaneously (naltrexone, acamprosate, disulfiram, gabapentin) plus psychiatric medications; he reported mixed benefit, imperfect adherence, and ongoing relapse despite overall tolerability. During admission, disulfiram was stopped and acamprosate/gabapentin were renally dose-adjusted. Due to repeated relapses and very high utilization, he was later placed on involuntary commitment with residential treatment followed by intensive outpatient care, and remained abstinent for at least six months.
